newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia govt appoints Telstra float team.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia govt appoints Telstra float team.

text.p: The Australian government appointed on Thursday a team of stockbrokers from around the world to manage the forthcoming sharemarket float of its wholly owned telecommunications carrier Telstra Corp.

Australian finance minister John Fahey said Australian brokers J.B Were & Son, U.S.-based CS First Boston and European based ABN AMRO/Rothschild have been appointed global co-ordinators for the government's sale of a third of its stake.
Fahey said J.B Were, Ord Minnett, CS First Boston, Goldman Sachs/Macquarie Bank, Daiwa, ABN AMRO/Rothschild and Deutsche Morgan Grenfell have been appointed joint lead managers.

"All appointments will be subject to satisfactory conclusion of contractural and fee negotiations in which the Commonwealth (federal government) will adopt stringent commercial and accountability principles," Fahey said in a statement.
Fahey said 30 firms were invited to lodge proposals for the lead roles in Telstra's proposed float and 29 replied.
He said 13 firms were shortlisted and interviewed.

The joint global co-ordinators role is to help prepare Telstra for sale and lead the global selling effort for Telstra shares, provide advice on all sale issues, such as marketing and offer structure, and to manage the sale project, he said.

"A strong selling syndicate highly focussed on this assignment and with complementary management, distribution, and advisory skills is being put in place to ensure the success of what will be one of the largest transactions of this type in the world this year," Fahey said.
The appointment of firms to other selling roles, including domestic and international co-lead managers, would be made closer to the sale date, he said.
Fahey said it was anticipated that all Australian brokers would have a role in this sale.
All global co-ordinators and lead managers will be eligible to have a selling role throughout the world.
Fahey said the joint lead managers would assist the global co-ordinators in selling in the various markets.

He said the government will now move to select an independent business adviser, without a selling role, domestic and international legal advisers, and accounting advisers to assist with the sale prepartions.
He said the global co-ordinators would assist the government to develop a detailed project plan, including advice on Telstra's capital structure and design of offer structure.
